curriculum_scope: LKS Cyber Security 2026 / NIST SP 800-115 / WorldSkills Skill 54

vulnerability.title: Even RSA Modulus Trivial Factorization
vulnerability.root_cause: The RSA key generation process fails to reject the even prime p=2, yielding an even composite modulus N (N % 2 == 0) that factors instantly via division by 2.
vulnerability.impact: Complete collapse of RSA confidentiality and total recovery of private exponent d.

remediation.primary: Enforce strict candidate prime range checking and Miller-Rabin primality testing ensuring p, q > 2 are distinct odd primes of at least 1024 bits.
remediation.standard: FIPS 186-5 Section A.1 / NIST SP 800-56B Rev. 2

modules.author: Brhane Giday and Prince Niyonshuti N.

vulnerability.title: Cleartext / Reversible Sensitive Flag Storage in HTTP Set-Cookie Header
vulnerability.root_cause: The web application stores the secret flag inside the Set-Cookie HTTP response header encoded only in Base64.
vulnerability.impact: Direct information disclosure of secret credentials/data to any unauthenticated client.

remediation.primary: Never store secret application data in client-side cookies. Implement server-side session stores with opaque high-entropy UUID session IDs and enforce HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite attributes.
remediation.standard: RFC 6265bis / OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet

vulnerability.title: Predictable PRNG Seeding via Millisecond Epoch Time
vulnerability.root_cause: Python standard random module (MT19937) is seeded with int(time.time() * 1000), reducing the key space to a tight millisecond window predictable from network connection time.
vulnerability.impact: Deterministic state recovery and authentication token spoofing within 50 attempts.

remediation.primary: Migrate from Mersenne Twister (random module) to Cryptographically Secure Pseudo-Random Number Generators (CSPRNG) such as Python's secrets module or os.urandom().
